description: The relations time slider: read every mark at one timestamp instead of reducing its rows to a stat. Deterministic TestData throughout — fixed epoch timestamps, so every panel looks the same twice.

panels.description:
**The ragged multi-frame shape, with the slider on.**

Three `csv_content` queries, one edge each, and — deliberately — **three different time columns**. `api-->db` starts one step late and `api-->cache` samples every other step, which is what a real response looks like when a series has a gap or a scrape is missed.

That raggedness is why the selection is a **timestamp** and not a slider index: row 2 is a different instant in each of these frames, so the timestamp is resolved to a row *per frame* (`graphWideTimeline` unions the stops; `rowAt` resolves each frame's own).

Drag the slider, arrow-key it or click a step button. Three things to look for:

- the edge weights change (they are drawn on the links — "Show edge values" is on);
- at the **first** stop `api-->db` has no sample at all, so it draws weightless rather than vanishing — the topology does not move while you scrub;
- the "Calculation" picker is gone from the Value options: at one selected row every reducer agrees, so there is nothing left to reduce — and a mark's tooltip labels its main row `Value` rather than `Last *`, for the same reason.

**The data link on `gateway-->api` is the fix you cannot see anywhere else.** Hover that edge and read the footer: `${__value.numeric}` interpolates the value at the **selected row**, so it now agrees with the tooltip. Under the reducer it could only ever point at row 0 — the oldest sample — because there is no one row a mean came from.
panels.title: Ragged ranged edges — one frame per edge, scrubbable

panels.description:
**The control: the same three frames, reduced.**

Identical data to the panel on its left, with the slider **off** — so the "Calculation" picker is back and `calcs[0]` (`Last *` by default) collapses each mark's whole timeline to one number.

Side by side these two are the choice this feature adds. The reducer answers "one number for the window"; the slider answers "the graph as it was at 00:05". Note that the slider's *default* position is the newest stop, which is exactly what `Last *` shows — so switching the option on changes no picture until you move it.

Switch the calculation to Max or Mean to see what the reducer can say that a single row cannot.
panels.title: The same edges, reduced by calcs[0] — no slider

panels.description:
**The pivoted shape: one wide frame, one shared row grid.**

This is what a real Prometheus or Loki range query becomes once `converters/longToWide.ts` has run above the panel — a single time field that is the ascending union of every series' timestamps, one numeric field per edge, `null` where a series has no sample.

The slider behaves identically. That is the point of testing both shapes: the row dimension is resolved per frame either way, so a response that shares one grid and a response that shares none step through the same stops.

A sankey, so the scrub is visible in the **geometry** rather than in a label: a ribbon's thickness is its weight, where a graph link's thickness comes from `custom.lineWidth`.

**It cuts rather than morphing, and that is ECharts'.** `SankeyView.render` writes every shape imperatively and has no diff against the previous render, so there is nothing to tween; the chord panel below shows what a morph looks like. See [todo/relations-scrub-animation.md](../../../todo/relations-scrub-animation.md) for the three fixes that were measured and rejected.
panels.title: One wide ranged frame (the pivoted shape) — sankey

panels.description:
**The negative case: the option on, against instant data.**

One row and no time column at all — the `csv_content` / `rowsToFields` / Tempo service-map route. There is nowhere to scrub to, so no strip is drawn and the plot keeps the whole panel.

Because the option *also* hides the "Calculation" picker, that would leave no control and no explanation — so the panel posts an advisory in its corner instead (hover the info icon).

The **switch itself** is hidden on data like this: open the editor and "Time slider" is absent from the Value options on a panel that never had it on. It stays visible here only because this panel does have it on — the escape hatch that keeps a refresh from stranding a panel with a hidden picker and no way back. `tempo-service-map.json` is the live version of this case; it is deliberately left alone.
panels.title: Instant data with the slider on — no strip, one advisory

panels.description:
**The one variant that morphs between stops.**

The same wide ranged frame as the sankey, drawn as a chord — and this is where a step *animates* rather than cutting. The difference is ECharts', not the panel's: `ChordView.render` diffs the new data against the old and updates each arc in place, so the arcs and ribbons tween. `SankeyView.render` sets every shape imperatively (`curve.setShape`) and has no diff at all, so a sankey redraws correctly but instantly. A `graph` tweens its node symbols, but a link's thickness comes from `custom.lineWidth` rather than from its weight, so on this data there is nothing there to move.

Use this panel to see what a scrub *is*; use the sankey to see the weights, which are easier to read as ribbons.
panels.title: The same wide frame as a chord — the variant that morphs
